options.name: Progression Balancing
options.doc:
A system that can move progression earlier, to try and prevent the player from getting stuck and bored early.

A lower setting means more getting stuck. A higher setting means less getting stuck.
options.doc_html:
A system that can move progression earlier, to try and prevent the player from getting stuck and bored early.

options.doc_fr:
Un système qui peut déplacer la progression plus tôt, pour essayer et empêcher le joueur de se coincer et s'ennuyer tôt.

Un réglage plus bas signifie qu'il reste coincé. Un réglage plus élevé signifie moins se coincer.

options.name: Accessibility
options.doc:
Set rules for reachability of your items/locations.

**Full:** ensure everything can be reached and acquired.

**Minimal:** ensure what is needed to reach your goal can be acquired.

options.name: Basic Research Location Count
options.doc: The number of basic research locations in the game. These will only require the basic research bench.

options.name: Hi-Tech Research Location Count
options.doc: The number of hi-tech research locations in the game. These will only require the hi-tech research bench (which requires Microelectronics.)

options.name: Multi-Analyzer Research Location Count
options.doc: The number of multi-analyzer research locations in the game. These will only require the hi-tech research bench and the multi-analyzer (and the research for them.)

options.name: Research Base Cost
options.doc: The amount of research points required to research research locations.

options.name: Research Cost Variance
options.doc:
The max amount research points will vary by for research locations.
If the base cost is 500 and the variance is 800, every research will cost between 500 and 1300 points.

options.name: Research Cost Increase Per Tier
options.doc:
The amount of points that will increase per research tier.
For example, if the base cost is 500, the variance is 800, and the Increase Per Tier is 100, a third-tier (third column) research will be
between 700 and 1500 points.

options.name: Research Max Prerequisites
options.doc: The max number of prerequisites for the generated Archipelago research. The higher this is, the more restricted your selection of research will be.

options.name: Craft Location Count
options.doc: The number of craft locations in the game. These locations require crafting two random items together.

options.name: Raid Location Count
options.doc: The number of raid locations in the game. These locations require defeating a target enemy, one of which will carry a location item in its inventory in each raid.

options.name: Trade Location Count
options.doc: The number of trade locations in the game. These locations require trading with a caravan or settlement for a location item.

options.name: Quest Location Count
options.doc: The number of quest locations in the game. These locations require completing a quest for a location item.

options.name: Raid Trap Count
options.doc: The guaranteed number of raid traps in the game.

options.name: Colonist Item Count
options.doc: The number of colonists that will get sent as items in the game. Note: If you wind up with more than ~20 colonists, you may have performance issues.

options.name: Use Player Names for Colonist Items
options.doc: If enabled, random player names from the multiworld will be used for colonist nicknames

options.name: Craft Location Count
options.doc: The chance random filler will become trap items, like raids.

options.name: Victory Condition
options.doc: The way to win. Choosing "any" will ensure one of these is considered "in-logic." They also require a "basic" set of research that isn't strictly required to win, so royalty will consider pianos and noble apparel in logic, while anomaly will consider basic bioferrite research in logic. The monument victory condition will require building a room with special archipelago statues and some number of randomized room conditions.

options.name: Monument Statue Count
options.doc: If the monument victory condition is enabled, this specifies how many Archipelago statues will be required to create a monument and win the game.

options.name: Extra Monument Statue Count
options.doc: If the monument victory condition is enabled, this specifies how many extra monument statues will be in the pool, allowing the player an easier victory.

options.name: Monument Other Building Requirement Count
options.doc: If the monument victory condition is enabled, this specifies how many non-statue building requirements will be required to create a monument and win the game.

options.name: MonumentWealthRequirement
options.doc: If the monument victory condition is enabled, this specifies how much wealth is required in the monument room to win.

options.name: Royalty Enabled
options.doc: Enable the Royalty DLC. If you disable any DLC in yaml and enable it in client, all research will be researchable and excluded from the generator.

options.name: Ideology Enabled
options.doc: Enable the Ideology DLC. If you disable any DLC in yaml and enable it in client, all research will be researchable and excluded from the generator.

options.name: Biotech Enabled
options.doc: Enable the Biotech DLC. If you disable any DLC in yaml and enable it in client, all research will be researchable and excluded from the generator.

options.name: Anomoly Enabled
options.doc: Enable the Anomaly DLC. If you disable any DLC in yaml and enable it in client, all research will be researchable and excluded from the generator.

options.name: Odyssey Enabled
options.doc: Enable the Odyssey DLC. If you disable any DLC in yaml and enable it in client, all research will be researchable and excluded from the generator.

options.name: Starting Research Level
options.doc: If "none" is selected, the player will have access to NO research, regardless of starting scenario. Tribal and Crashlanded will give the player those starting research (regardless of starting scenario.)

options.name: Bonus Research Items
options.doc: How many bonus items will you receive when a research (that unlocks items) is received. For example, if this is set to 2, you may receive a jacket and a flophat when you receive Complex Clothing. If set to -1, you'll receive one of everything, otherwise, you'll receive any number at random (note: This means setting it to higher than 1 may result in getting, say, 5 Harps when you receive Harp.)

options.name: ResearchScoutType
options.doc: How research project scouting works - this will show you what items research projects will send. "None" will show no information for all research. "Summary" options will show the player name and item type (Chris's progressive item). "Fullitem" options will show player name and item name (Chris's progressive item, Master Sword). "Available" options will show only if the research can be started now. "All" options will hint all research.

options.name: ResearchScoutSecretTraps
options.doc: If turned on, the game will lie about scouted trap items. If the scout type shows the player and item name, all traps will be replaced by a random progression item from another player (instead of showing Alex's freeze trap, it will show Chris's Master Sword.) If the scout type only shows item type, it will simply show traps as progression items.

options.name: Neolithic Item Weight
options.doc: How likely it will be that low/no-tech items are chosen for crafting locations. Higher weights make this category more likely. 0 will exempt it from the list. Note that these categories are slightly different than the vanilla "Tech Level," to help account for how challenging they are to craft.

options.name: Medieval Item Weight
options.doc: How likely it will be that low-tech items are chosen for crafting locations. Higher weights make this category more likely. 0 will exempt it from the list. Note that these categories are slightly different than the vanilla "Tech Level," to help account for how challenging they are to craft.

options.name: Industrial Item Weight
options.doc: How likely it will be that mid-tech items are chosen for crafting locations. Higher weights make this category more likely. 0 will exempt it from the list. Note that these categories are slightly different than the vanilla "Tech Level," to help account for how challenging they are to craft.

options.name: Spacer Item Weight
options.doc: How likely it will be that high-tech items are chosen for crafting locations. Higher weights make this category more likely. 0 will exempt it from the list. Note that these categories are slightly different than the vanilla "Tech Level," to help account for how challenging they are to craft.

options.name: Hard To Make Item Weight
options.doc: How likely it will be that complicated items are chosen for crafting locations. These items usually require specific/unique investment, like multiple advanced components and the like. Higher weights make this category more likely. 0 will exempt it from the list. Note that these categories are slightly different than the vanilla "Tech Level," to help account for how challenging they are to craft.

options.name: Anomaly Item Weight
options.doc: How likely it will be that Anomaly-specific items are chosen for crafting locations. These items will often require bioferrite, and investment into the anomaly expansion to craft. Higher weights make this category more likely. 0 will exempt it from the list. Note that these categories are slightly different than the vanilla "Tech Level," to help account for how challenging they are to craft.

options.name: Death Link
